Marina — thanks, helpful feedback. Short answers up front: (1) HSM terminates in the control-plane subnet on a management VLAN with a separate mgmt NIC; we will use a dedicated tunnel to the customer's KMS gateway (no plaintext keys across data plane). (2) Telemetry egress will be restricted to a single collector IP via an egress proxy and TLS; no telemetry flows out directly from worker nodes.

I've attached an updated diagram (redwood_onprem_boundary_v1.drawio.png) showing the HSM termination and the egress proxy. Also included a control/data-plane mapping spreadsheet (controlplane_dataplane_matrix_v3.xlsx) with the proposed ACLs.

Quick technical notes from my side before the call:

- Control plane hosts run in a separate subnet (Mgmt-VLAN) and are reachable only from the customer admin CIDR and our ops jump-hosts. We recommend a small set of public IPs for the control-plane NAT; these are only used for patch management and not for data-plane traffic.
- Data plane (worker/GPU) nodes are fully isolated in an internal VLAN. No direct inbound from customer networks except through the service-facing LB.
- We suggest an eBPF-based ingress proxy on the worker hosts for workload-level traffic shaping and to capture prefix cache metrics. This avoids adding a separate sidecar to each model process.
- For logging/telemetry, we will mirror logs to a local syslog endpoint and then forward a filtered subset to the SIEM via the egress proxy.

I'll bring a short checklist to the meeting: firewall rules, NAT ranges, jump-host hardening, and cert rotation cadence.

—Aditya

Thanks for the diagram and the call today — useful session. A couple of follow-ups from our side:

- On the control-plane/data-plane demarcation, we recommend adding a tiny bastion VPC that sits in the customer management plane and performs certificate-based auth to the control-plane APIs. This reduces reliance on IP allowlists for operator access.
- For the KMS integration: we can support a TLS-mutual-auth flow to the customer's HSM gateway; however, ACME's HSM only permits connections from a single source IP. If Redwood's control-plane uses autoscaling pools, we'd need a stable egress IP — recommend a NAT-VM or SNAT appliance placed in the mgmt VLAN.
- Suggested action: capture the NAT egress IP need in the controlplane_dataplane_matrix_v3.xlsx under 'operational_prereqs'.

We'll prepare a short runbook snippet that maps operational tasks to parties (ACME ops / Redwood infra / CloudPartner). Will share by EOD tomorrow.

—Ethan (CloudPartner Solutions)
